actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The core installation includes MuJoCo, OpenCV and NumPy
The project requires Python 3.8 or newer
The package declares mujoco 3.2.0 or newer as a core dependency
MMK2Cfg names the MJCF scene mjcf/mmk2_floor.xml
MMK2Cfg sets the timestep to 0.0025 s and the decimation to 4
MMK2Base declares 28 qpos and 19 control values for the scene
MMK2Cfg's init_state gives the base position and orientation and zero positions for the slide, head, arm and gripper joints
SimulatorBase copies config.timestep onto model.opt.timestep after loading the model
SimulatorBase sets delta_t to the model timestep times the decimation
SimulatorBase.step runs updateControl and mj_step decimation times per call
The scene is the MJCF model named mmk2
The scene includes mmk2_options.xml and mmk2_dependencies.xml
The scene adds a plane geom named floor
The scene attaches a body named mmk2 to the world with an unnamed free joint
The scene includes mobile_chassis/mmk2/mmk2.xml inside that body
The scene's actuator section includes mmk2_control.xml
The scene's sensor section includes mmk2_sensor.xml
The scene has a home keyframe with 28 qpos values
The included options set the RK4 integrator and the Newton solver and state no timestep
The dependencies include the Airbot Play dependency file
The slide_joint default gives the lift the joint range -0.04 to 0.87 m and the position actuator the same ctrlrange with kp 50000
The head yaw joint range is -0.5 to 0.5 rad and the head pitch joint range is -1.18 to 0.16 rad, with matching position ctrlranges
The wheel default gives both wheel motors the ctrlrange and forcerange -35 to 35
The control fragment declares two wheel motors, the lift, head yaw and head pitch, and seven position actuators per arm
The two gripper position actuators have the ctrlrange 0 to 1
The Airbot Play joint ctrlranges are joint1 -3.151 to 2.089, joint2 -2.963 to 0.181, joint3 -0.094 to 3.161, joint4 -3.012 to 3.012, joint5 -1.859 to 1.859 and joint6 -3.017 to 3.017 rad
The sensor fragment publishes joint positions, tendon positions, joint velocities and tendon velocities for the controlled joints

determinism.notes: the model has no random element and MuJoCo integrates it deterministically from the reset state, so the same ctrl sequence and tick count repeat a trajectory; the package's stand-in is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the scene and its includes for the 28 qpos, 27 dof, 19 actuators and their control ranges, then moves each actuated joint toward its control value; it computes no inertias, contacts, tendons, equalities or actuator and sensor dynamics, so no trajectory here is a MuJoCo result
the meshes and textures are not loaded by the stand-in; a real engine load needs them beside the model, which the pinned clone provides

the model file states no <option timestep>; MMK2Cfg sets 0.0025 s and SimulatorBase copies it onto the model, but this package loads the model file directly and does not apply that configuration.  The reference's timestep_ms (2.0) is the library default supplied by the stand-in's placeholder fallback, not a value stated by the model

the bridge's reset calls mj_resetData and starts from the model defaults, not from the upstream init_state or the home keyframe of mmk2_floor.xml:37-38; a client that wants a pose must send its ctrl and step

the upstream step applies the action for decimation=4 substeps (mmk2_base.py:10 and simulator.py:639-642); the bridge applies ctrl at every tick with no decimation, so one bridge tick is one mj_step, not one upstream step
the upstream updateControl path clips a control to the actuator ctrlrange; the bridge refuses an out-of-range ctrl before writing it, which is the safer direction but a different contract
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time by the model's timestep only
no rendering, cameras or sensor publication: the 19 joint sensors are not exposed as an observation, only the bridge's time, qpos, qvel and ctrl state is
the model is a simulation asset for the MMK2: no physical robot is modelled or controlled and nothing here was validated against the hardware

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
